text:
anya: Heads-up — I'm assembling the calibration prompt set for the upcoming AWQ / GPTQ bakeoff. Goal: a single canonical calib set that exercises diversity (length, domains, languages), failure modes, and structured outputs. Thinking buckets: short Q/A, multi-turn chat, code completions, math, tables/csv parsing, hallucination-prone, low-resource languages, and adversarial paraphrases. Target ~5k total but with smaller dev slices (500-1k) for fast iter ops.

kevin: +1. Would add an explicit "format-sensitive" bucket for function-calling / JSON outputs — small syntactic changes break some quant formats. Also: preserve tokenization distribution (median/90th pct) so runtime seq len matches production. :+1: 

jasmin: Quick q: how do you want to sample per-bucket? stratified by domain + length? random-with-seed? we should keep deterministic runs for replaying regressions.

anya: Yup — stratified sampling. Proposal: define buckets by (domain, answer_type, token_len_bucket). For each bucket sample N with seed. Default seed=42 for initial run; keep the seed in filenames. Example plan: 10 buckets x 500 each = 5k. For faster experiments, generate 3 dev folds 200 each.

kevin: Here's a small script snippet I ran locally for deterministic sampling: 
```bash
python tools/sample_calib.py \
  --input datasets/master_prompts.csv \
  --schema buckets.yaml \
  --seed 42 \
  --per-bucket 500 \
  --out calib/awq_gptq_seed42.jsonl
```
The script also emits a CSV with bucket counts + token len hist.

taylor: Important: for few-shot vs zero-shot we should preserve the 'prefix' tokens used in production prompts. If we strip few-shot examples for calibration we might miss KV cache interactions that affect quant behavior. Suggest two parallel variants: +ctx (keep few-shot examples) and -ctx (zero-shot). Compare deltas.

jasmin: For multilingual buckets: include at least 200 examples total across es/fr/pt/zh/ru + 50 in a couple low-resource langs (sw, hi). Don't overrepresent en. Also include code-switching examples.

anya: Agreed. Also adding an "edge-case" minibatch: 200 paraphrase adversarials generated by a paraphrase model (theta-paraphrase-v1) with BLEU < 0.6 wrt original to catch brittle token-level quant errors.

kevin: On metrics: we'll compute per-example "answer equivalence" (normalized string match), exact-match for structured outputs, EM for closed QA, and token-level NLL delta between FP16 baseline and quant variant. I also want a small automated diff that flags any example with >2% token-nll increase or answer mismatch.

anya: Rule of thumb: if a quant config causes >1% absolute drop in global accuracy on the full calib set OR any bucket shows >3% drop, we treat as a regression and block rollout to that deployment profile. That threshold is conservative but helps avoid surprising user regressions.

jasmin: For gating, we should produce a per-bucket report with: count, baseline-acc, quant-acc, acc-delta, avg-token-nll-delta, top-10 worst examples (with inputs/outputs). That helps debugging and PR triage.

calib-bot: Deploy plan saved: calib/sets/awq_gptq_seed42/metadata.json (includes seed, buckets.yaml, generated_at).

taylor: Small nit on prompts: keep instruction tone variants (imperative, request, question) because some models respond differently and quant changes can amplify that. Also include 1% of very long-context (4-8k tokens) samples to stress kv-cache.

kevin: For the bakeoff matrix let's run: FP16 baseline, AWQ int8, GPTQ-4bit, FP8 (where available) across two serving profiles (low-latency small-batch, high-throughput batching). Compare throughput & QPS vs accuracy deltas. We'll record rollout_profile tags in the results.

anya: I'll generate initial calib sets tonight and post links. Please review the buckets.yaml and the sample manifest before I land it. If nobody objects I'll lock seeds and run the first sweep tomorrow morning.

jasmin: Thanks — will add 200 adversarial paraphrases and a 100-example "synthesis-of-hallucination" set (contradictory context + question).

kevin: One last thing: include an "inspect-only" mode that outputs tokenization / byte-level diffs for the top-20 failed examples. Those diffs help trace quant behavior tied to kernel edge cases.

anya: Perfect. tagging @taylor for few-shot contexts. Will post the calib manifest here when ready. :rocket:
